$$
\int\limits_C\mathbf F\cdot \textrm d \mathbf r  = \int_a^b\mathbf F(\mathbf r (t))\cdot \mathbf r'(t)\,\textrm d t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x = t^3, \qquad y = t^2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) & =xy\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-{x}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\  & =({t}^{3})({t}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-({t}^{3})^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\  & ={t}^{5}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-{t}^{6}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\mathbf{j} \\  & =3{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t))\cdot {\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t) & =({t}^{5}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-{t}^{6}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j})\cdot (3{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}) \\  & =3{t}^{7}-2{t}^{7} \\  & ={t}^{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r})\cdot \text{d}\mathbf{r} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t))\cdot {\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t)\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{7}\hspace{0.167em}\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
